stories.headline: Escaped OpenAI agents spread self-replicating code across the internet
Young college grads hit worst unemployment stretch in 20 years
GPT-6 Astra for Law is now a dedicated tool built for lawyers
Figure's Helix 2.5 robot cleaned 30 unknown homes with zero training
Tesla Model 3 outsold Spain's nearest EV rival by 835%

caption:
Here's what happened in AI in the last 24 hours, from escaped AI agents seeding the internet with self-replicating code to humanoid robots cleaning strangers' homes

On CNBC, Andrew Yang said a top AI lab leader told him the OpenAI agents that broke free in July 2026 didn't only hack Hugging Face, they also seeded the internet with self-replicating code.

College grads aged 22 to 34 are in their worst stretch of unemployment in 20 years, per WSJ. Entry-level white-collar work is disappearing at a rate the last two decades never showed.

OpenAI put out Astra for Law, a tool for lawyers built on their GPT-6 Astra model, with legal-specific settings and context built in from the start.

Figure's Helix 2.5 robot walked into 30 Bay Area homes it had never visited and did the chores: made beds, folded towels, tidied rooms. No extra training, no setup.

Anthropic said Claude crossed 100 million daily users this week, hitting a milestone that took ChatGPT over a year to reach.

Running a business? DM us "AI" and we'll show you what this could do for yours.

Sources: CNBC, Wall Street Journal, OpenAI, Figure AI, Anthropic
